lots.guide_summary: All evidence is Gowans SOLD hammers, AUD, no conversion. Close entries (Trax Holden boxed singles and pairs) run $40 to $80 per lot, which is roughly $20 to $45 per model. Single Holden models of mixed brands run $25 to $55. On that basis this five-model lot would likely hammer around $100 to $180. No unsold or asking evidence. No Armitage past results (web search budget exhausted).
lots.working: No sale of this exact five-model lot exists, so the maximum is built up per model from close SOLD entries. Lowest per-model close sale: Trax 3-model FJ set plus Siku car $62, which is under $21 per model; take $20 per model x 5 = $100. keep_max_hammer = 100 / 1.22 = 81.97, rounded down to $80 (all-in $97.60). Flip: likely resale about 5 x $30 = $150 at a Tasmanian auction, less 20% seller commission ($30), $0 postage (sold locally) = $120; 120 / 2.44 = 49.2, rounded down to $45. The margin on a flip is thin.
lots.confidence_reason: Only one box (Trax) is read clearly. Brands of the other four are unread at this resolution, though the perspex cases with printed info cards look like Classic Carlectables or similar. No sale of the same lot; maximum rests on per-model build-up from close Gowans pairs and singles opened via the API.
lots.dropped_entries: None dropped. The researcher's grouped entries (382501/382503 and 432462/432464) were split or noted separately. Verifier added 422781 Trax HQ Monaro $45.
lots.key_photo_findings: Trax logo on the top-left case (cream sedan). Green wagon case reads '... Classic Model' with an oval logo, brand unread. Three bottom cases have black plinths with printed info cards: 'HOLDEN 48-215 SEDAN, Released September 1948', 'HOLDEN ... (wagon)', 'HOLDEN FJ ... Released July 1953' style text; a small logo on the base of the taxi case may be a maker mark. Perspex cases look intact, models appear clean, no visible damage. Outer cardboard sleeves not shown.
lots.condition: Appears very good: models clean in display cases, no visible damage. Outer card boxes or sleeves not shown and certificates unknown.
lots.question_for_armitage: What brand are the four non-Trax models (check the base of each case and the info card, for example Classic Carlectables or Trax)? Are the outer cardboard boxes or sleeves present, and are any cases cracked or models loose from their plinths?

lots.working: No SOLD evidence for a DJI Neo, so keep_max_hammer = 0 and flip_max_hammer = 0. The only price is a new retail asking price (USD 169, about AUD 260 at an assumed 0.65), which cannot set a maximum.
lots.confidence_reason: Identification is clear from the box and body marking, but the only price is a retail asking price, battery presence is unknown and the drone's function is untested.
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped all six Gowans SOLD entries as comparables (DJI Phantom 3 $30 lot 377893; Phantom 2 with screen $130 lot 378966; Phantom 4 unused $290 lot 385606; Mavic 3 mixed lot $220 lot 377441; Holy Stone HS900 $110 lot 434336; Holy Stone HS360D $55 lot 442305). The records are real (API opened, prices and dates match) but they are different models or brands, not the same item, so they only show that the local pool pays $30 to $290 for drones. The researcher's AUD 260 figure on the DJI page relied on an assumed rate; kept as ASKING with that caveat.
lots.key_photo_findings: Box clearly reads 'dji NEO' with Armitage lot label 1473 and handwritten 'S186/16'. Drone body marked NEO and DJI logo, prop guards intact, gimbal/camera cover looks clean. Accessories: two bags of spare propellers, screwdriver, USB-C to USB-C cable, quick start guide. The rear of the drone (where the battery sits) is not shown, so whether the battery is fitted cannot be confirmed. No remote controller, no charging hub.
lots.condition: Looks clean and lightly used or near new in photos. Battery presence, charge and function unknown. Not tested.
lots.question_for_armitage: Is the Intelligent Flight Battery fitted in the drone (check the rear)? Does it power on and charge? Is it unlinked from any previous owner's DJI account? Any crash damage to the guards or camera?
